The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Public
Safety Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 3rd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the American Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires
modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Fire
Department at (626) 300­0735 or at fire@cityofsanmarino.org at least 48 hours prior to the
meeting.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do it’s best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Public Safety
Commission by completing a public comment card prior to the meeting. At this time, the
public may address the Public Safety Commission on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the Public Safety Commission may not discuss or take action on
issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.3). The Chair reserves
the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such
items.

BACKGROUND

Each month, the San Marino Police Department provides a brief and
informational update on crime, traffic issues, and other items of interest to
the public and to the Public Safety Commission.

DISCUSSION

Significant Incidents
Domestic Violence / Battery
July 6, 2023, officers were dispatched to the area of St Albans Road and Mill
Lane regarding a male who was requesting police and then disconnected.
Officer’s later made contact with the reporting party, the suspect, and a
female near the area. It was determined the victim and suspect were in a
dating relationship, and a physical altercation occurred between the two. The
reporting party was a friend who witnessed the physical altercation. During
the altercation, the witness attempted to help the victim, and was hit in the
head by the suspect. Based on the witness statements and physical evidence,
suspect William Mathew Walling (DOB 04/30/1968, Sun Valley, CA) was
placed under arrest for PC 273.5/domestic violence and PC 242/battery.

  PAGE 4 of 44
 Wanted Felony Vehicle and Person
July 7, 2023, Officers received notification of a wanted vehicle in the area of
Huntington Drive and Virginia Road. The vehicle was wanted by Los Angeles
Police Department. Officers at the intersection of Huntington Drive and San
Marino Avenue located the vehicle. A felony traffic stop was conducted in a
parking lot near the intersection of Sierra Madre Boulevard and San Pasqual
Street. The driver of the vehicle was subsequently detained until LAPD arrived
on scene and took custody of the suspect and the vehicle in question.

Incident Report
July, 30, 2023 SMPD Officers were advised of a suspect that had pointed a
handgun at multiple victims in the City of Pasadena. Pasadena PD provided
the suspect and suspect vehicle descriptions. A SMPD officer observed the
suspect’s vehicle in the area of Huntington Drive and Oak Knoll Avenue and
conducted a high-risk traffic stop. A vehicle search revealed a loaded 9 MM
handgun. The suspect, Scotty Lu Wells Jr. (DOB 04/07/00 San Gabriel, CA)
was taken into custody.

Stolen Vehicle
August 15, 2023 a vehicle that was left unlocked was reported stolen from the
1700 block of Banning Way. Due to a time delay no suspects were located at
the time of call.

Recovered Stolen Vehicle
August 19, 2023 San Marino Police Department received a notification of a
stolen vehicle in the 1400 block of Wilson Avenue. When the Officers located
the vehicle it was unoccupied. The registered owner requested the vehicle to
be towed.

Stolen Vehicle
August 19, 2023, a vehicle that was unsecured with keys on the front seat
was stolen from the 2100 block of Valentine Place.

Robbery
August 21, 2023, The suspect unsuccessfully attempted to grab the victim’s
cross body purse, however forcefully grabbed cash from the victim’s hand,
and fled the scene.

Assault with a Deadly Weapon / Battery on a Peace Officers
August 24, 2023, Officers responded to the above location regarding a verbal
argument and a man with a knife. The suspect was identified as Alexander
John Hendry (DOB 11/01/1989 San Marino, CA). Hendry was taken into
custody for various charges including domestic violence making criminal
threats, assault with a deadly weapon (a knife), battery on peace officers,

  PAGE 5 of 44
 obstruction/resisting an officer, and other offenses against officers and
emergency personnel. Subsequently, Hendry was transported to the Pasadena
City Jail for booking.

Search Warrant
August 28, 2023, SMPD conducted a search warrant in the City of South
Pasadena and the City of San Marino for a residence and business related to
an embezzlement case.

Stolen Vehicle / Pursuit
September 09, 2023, SMPD received an alert for a stolen vehicle in the area
of Huntington Drive and Granada Avenue. Officers located the vehicle and it
fled at a high rate of speed. The vehicle came to a stop and suspect foot bailed
into the 2500 block of Melville Drive. The officer pursued the suspect and lost
sight. The passenger of the vehicle identified herself and the suspect as
juveniles. The passenger was transported home and released to her parents.
This investigation was

Stolen Vehicle
September 18, 2023, The San Marino Police Department was notified of a
stolen vehicle within the city limits. The vehicle was located and a high-risk
traffic enforcement stop was conducted. A records check revealed the driver
Carlos Arias (DOB 10/31/1986, Los Angeles, CA) had three outstanding
warrants for his arrest out of the Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department and the
San Bernardino Sheriff’s Department. The passenger Luis Sosa (DOB
11/07/1990, Pasadena, CA) returned with no warrants. Both suspects were
taken into custody, and transported to the Pasadena City Jail. The stolen
vehicle was released to the registered owner at the scene.

Detective Bureau / Investigations
Over the months of July to September of 2023, the Detective Bureau
completed the following activities:

•  Detectives authored four search warrants over this time period. Search
warrants were executed for a residence and business involved in an
embezzlement investigation. A follow up search warrant was also executed
for electronic devices related to the embezzlement investigation. Additionally,
a search warrant was executed at a residence for property for safekeeping
due to a related call for service.

•  Detectives provided community outreach and crime prevention
information to a jewelry store located in town. The storeowner was concerned
due to “smash and grab” commercially robberies throughout the county.

  PAGE 6 of 44
 •  In the month of July, detectives conducted follow up investigation on a
missing adult. Detectives were able to obtain GPS pings for the subject’s cell
phone. Detectives were able to locate the missing adult within Los Angeles
County. The subject was found safe and in good health.

•  Newly assigned Detective Burgos completed the two-week detective
school program.

•  During the above time period, 32 cases were filed with the district
attorney’s office.

•  There 113 FLOCK camera alert notifications. As a result, five of these
FLOCK notifications resulted in arrests.

In July to September of 2023, there were sixteen residential burglary
investigations - four were reported in July, seven were reported in August,
and four were reported in September. There may have been an increase in
burglaries over the summer due to vacant homes caused by summer
vacations. The majority of these homes had rear doors or windows shattered
for suspects to gain entry into the homes. Approximately half of these homes
had surveillance videos and many did not have alarm systems at their
residence.

Personnel
The Police Department currently has 30 sworn positions filled. We continue to
pursue interested police officer applicants to fill the two vacant positions. One
lateral police officer applicant is currently in the background process. Police
Officer Recruit candidates will be interviewed in the coming weeks.

All Police Dispatcher positions have been filled. The two newest Police
Dispatchers are currently on training.

We have one vacant part-time Records Clerk and a Management Analyst
position that are open. The Records Manager is working with the Human
Resources Director to establish a class specification for the part-time records
clerk position to begin recruiting. Applications have been reviewed and
interviews will be conducted by the Police Chief for the Management Analyst
position.

Technology
The deployment of new Flock cameras has begun. Approximately three new
cameras have been installed and are operational. The remaining six cameras
are in various stages of the deployment process. This includes a survey of the
intended area for utilities, potential obstructions, and available sunlight. The
Flock cameras continue to aid in the recovery of felony-stolen vehicles, and
be a useful investigative tool.

The Police Department has tested / evaluated AXON Body Worn Cameras
(BWC’s) and are currently being field-tested. Police Department Staff will be
meeting with Motorola in October for a demo of their BWC’s.

Traffic Enforcement
Traffic enforcement is based upon three categories; traffic complaints from
the community, observation of violations by officers, and traffic collision data.
The Department maintains a list of traffic complaint locations and traffic
collision data for traffic enforcement. As part of our traffic collision
investigations, we will look for other issues that may have been a contributory
factor in the collision. Those factors could be distracted driving, engineering,
or environmental. The City has two radar trailer that are deployed in problem
areas throughout the city, Radar trailer are used to reduce traffic speeds by
making drivers aware of how fast they are moving relative to the speed
limit. Our total number of citations issued for the month of July through
September is 617. Attached is a statistical report with information regarding
the collisions that occurred in the month July, August, and September.

Traffic Complaints
At the intersection of Old Mill and El Molino we received a complaint of Stop

Speeding and Stop Sign violations from 2:30 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. were reported
in the area of Bradbury and Melville. There has been nine traffic enforcements
conducted at the location since the complaint.

Vehicles parked in red zones, running stop signs, illegal U-turns, and speeding
were reported between the hours of 8:00 AM – 8:15 AM and 2:10 PM – 2:30
PM. Sherwood behind 1700 Huntington. There has been two traffic complaints
conducted since the complaint.

Stop sign violations were reported in the area of Lorain and San Marino. There
has been two traffic complaints conducted since the complaint.

Los Angeles County Court Zero Bail Program
This policy was instituted by the Presiding Judge and will be effective on

  PAGE 10 of 44
 October 1, 2023. Los Angeles County is the only county in the State to have
such a policy. This policy will result in a change for your police department
regarding the arrest protocols of individuals involved in criminal activity. As
the press release indicates, law enforcement must Cite and Release or Book
and Release arrestees in nearly all theft offenses, vehicle code violations, and
crimes against property such as petty theft, and vandalism. Offenses involving
guns, sexual battery, crimes against children/ elders and contact with minors
with intent to commit a sexual offense are examples of offenses subject to
Magistrate Review.

As an example of this change, a person arrested for False Imprisonment under
this new protocol would be eligible for book and release. Under the previous
bail schedule, their bail amount would be $50,000. Likewise, a person arrested
for theft of an automobile is eligible for book and release, while under the
previous bail schedule, their bail amount would be $35,000. All cite and
release arrests will occur at the place of arrest. Once cited by the arresting
officer the suspect will be released from that location. When a Magistrate
Review is appropriate, the officers will have approximately four hours to
complete their investigation and reports for submission to the Magistrate for
review. The Magistrates reviewing these arrests are current judges within the
Los Angeles County Court system.

BACKGROUND

The San Marino Fire Department completes a monthly report for the Public
Safety Commission, providing an overview of department activities, significant
incidents, and monthly statistics.

DISCUSSION

Significant Incidents
On Sunday October 1, 2023 at approximately2:20 PM a first alarm dispatch,
including Engine 91 and Battalion 9, responded to a multi-family dwelling
apartment fire in the city of South Pasadena. South Pasadena Engine 81
arrived first on scene to find smoke and fire from a two-story apartment
building. Engine 91 arrived second on scene and was attacked the fire with
Engine 81. Battalion 9 established command and called for a additional
resources due to the size of the fire and potential for victims. The blaze was
under control in approximately 20 minutes. The cause of the fire was
determined to be burning incense too close to easily ignited fuels. The
occupant fanned the flames in an attempt to put out the fire but rather spread
the fire. The involved apartment sustained heavy smoke and fire damage. All
other apartments had extensive smoke damage.

  PAGE 25 of 44
 Personnel
On Thursday, September 21 the San Marino Rotary Club recognized
Firefighter/Paramedic Brian Campbell and Officer Leroy Avington as the
Firefighter and Police Officer of the Year. The recognition was held at the San
Marino Fire Department and featured speeches by Rotary President Barbara
Bice, Rotary Member Maurice Saldebar, Fire Chief Mario Rueda, Police Chief
John Incontro, and Mayor Steve Talt. Firefighter/Paramedic Brian Campbell
was overwhelmingly nominated by his peers as this year’s Firefighter of the
Year. In addition to his role as a Firefighter/Paramedic, Firefighter Campbell
is also one of two Acting Engineers. In 2022, he received his State Fire Training
Instructor I certificate, and completed the inaugural Los Angeles Regional
Training Group Advanced Engine Operations course, from which he
implemented many new strategies and tactics into the department's training
manual. In April 2023, Firefighter Campbell celebrated his 11th employment
anniversary with the San Marino Fire Department. Thank you, Firefighter
Campbell, for all of your hard work and dedication to the department.

The Fire Department is currently recruiting for the position of Firefighter /
Paramedic. Applications are available at
https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/sanmarinoca. Applicants must
have a current State of California EMT-P license and Firefighter 1 certification
or completion of a fire academy.

On Monday, October 9 candidates completed the written portion of the
department’s Captain’s examination. The department has one vacancy at the
Captain’s position. The Fire Department receive received seven applications
from current San Marino Fire Department employees. The manipulative and
oral portions of the examination will be conducted on Monday, October 16.

Inspections
The San Marino Fire Department recently held an annual inspection of the
Department’s personnel, apparatus, equipment, and facilities. The inspection
was completed over the course of three days and involved weeks of
preparation by the Department’s on-duty personnel. The inspection was
overseen by Fire Chief Mario Rueda with the assistance of Division Chiefs Mark
Dondanville and Eric Zanteson. The annual inspection ensures the readiness
of the fire department and maintains operational standards of vehicles and
equipment.

Community
The San Marino Fire Department provided in-service fire life safety training for
the staff of Carver, Huntington Middle School, and Valentine. The training
included bleeding control, use of tourniquets, automatic external defibrillators,

  PAGE 26 of 44
 CPR and live fire training. Training for San Marino High School staff is
scheduled for later in October.

The Fire Department recently visited Carver Elementary’s second grade
classrooms and provided a fire safety demonstration as part of Fire Prevention
Month.

The Great ShakeOut
The Fire Department and executive staff are preparing for the annual Great
ShakeOut drill to be held on October 19, 2023. The Great ShakeOut is an
annual earthquake preparedness drill practiced by individuals, schools,
businesses, and government organizations on the third Thursday of October
each year. San Marino executive staff participated in a pre-drill training
exercise in September to coordinate each department’s responsibility prior to
the drill in October. The exercise presented executive staff with an overview
of the City’s emergency protocols in the event of a damaging earthquake. It
also covered specific earthquake threats to our region due to proximity to the
Raymond Fault, the Sierra Madre Fault, and the San Andreas Fault. In 2021,
the City of San Marino developed an Earthquake Operations Annex to the
City’s Emergency Operations Plan. The Earthquake Operations Annex provides
specific guidance and protocols for City staff in the event of an earthquake
affecting the City.

Family Assistance Center Annex to the Emergency Operations Plan
The San Marino Fire Department is in the process of preparing an annex to
the City’s Emergency Operations Plan for immediate family support in
response to mass casualty events. Chiefs Rueda and Incontro along with
Chiefs from neighboring agencies recently held discussions with Monterey Park
officials, including their City Attorney, regarding the post incident impacts of
the mass shooting. This included lessons learned from the activation of the
family assistance center in response to the active shooter event on January
21, 2023. The insights gained from these conversations will be integrated into
the City of San Marino’s plan.

Update to the Local Hazard Mitigation Plan
A local hazard mitigation plan (LHMP) is a comprehensive strategy developed
by state and local governments to identify natural and man-made disaster
risks and vulnerabilities common within a specific region. The goal of an LHMP
is to reduce loss of life and property by minimizing the impact of disasters.
FEMA requires that municipalities update their LHMP every 5 years; the City
of San Marino’s Local Hazard Mitigation was completed and approved by FEMA
on February 22, 2019. Staff recently issued a request for proposals for
contractors to update the plan. Responses to the RFP are due on Friday,
November 3.

  PAGE 27 of 44
 SCBA Replacement
The Fire Department is currently in the process of replacing the department’s
self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) equipment. The purchase of new
SCBA equipment and an air compressor/fill station was approved as part of
the FY 2023-24 Budget and the department anticipates presenting the
purchase for final City Council approval at the December 13 City Council
meeting. The purchase of new SCBA for all personnel will ensure that the
department’s equipment is compliant with NFPA standards during emergency
response situations. SCBAs are critical equipment for fire rescue operations
that require daily equipment checks and annual maintenance to ensure
operability. The department currently has 19 SCBAs and 60 cylinders
purchased in 2010 that have reached the end of their service life and are now
two cycles out of compliance with NFPA standards.

Training
Most recently, the San Marino Fire Department hosted fire personnel from
throughout the San Gabriel Valley for emergency incident, command
simulation training. Command simulation training provides a virtual scenario
in which Fire Department personnel act out command of an emergency
incident such as structure fires, hazardous materials release incidents,
wildland fires, violent incidents, etc. in real time with video and live dispatch
of the event. Participants are then able to review their response with training
staff to critique and provide areas for improvement.
